card.description:
Cargill is committed to providing food and agricultural solutions to nourish the world in a safe, responsible, and sustainable way. Sitting at the heart of the supply chain, we partner with farmers and customers to source, make and deliver products that are vital for living. 
Our 155,000 team members innovate with purpose, providing customers with life’s essentials so businesses can grow, communities prosper, and consumers live well. With over 160 years of experience as a family company, we look ahead while remaining true to our values. We put people first. We reach higher. We do the right thing—today and for generations to come.

**Location**
------------

This role will be based in one of the following locations:

* Wayzata, MN
* Atlanta, GA
* Wichita, KS

**Job Purpose and Impact**
--------------------------

The NA Regional Talent Acquisition Director leads a regional team responsible for the strategy, delivery, and continuous evolution of professional hiring for Food roles across NA. This role defines and executes a multi-year talent acquisition strategy aligned to business priorities, workforce plans, and growth objectives, ensuring the organization attracts, selects, and hires high-quality talent in a scalable, cost-effective manner.

This role partners closely with senior business leaders, HR leaders, and cross-functional stakeholders across the region to shape workforce strategies, provide market-informed insights, and deliver hiring outcomes that enable business growth. As a trusted advisor, the Director influences talent decisions through labor market intelligence, workforce analytics, and data-driven recommendations, ensuring talent acquisition is positioned as a strategic partner to the business.

The Director balances strategic vision with operational rigor, leveraging data, technology, and market intelligence to improve hiring speed, quality, diversity, candidate experience, and recruiter performance across the region while building capabilities for future workforce needs.

**Key Accountabilities**
------------------------

* STRATEGY DEVELOPMENT & EXECUTION: Leads NA talent acquisition strategy for Food, aligning recruiting priorities to business objectives, workforce plans, organizational capability needs, and future growth requirements. Partners with business and HR leaders to influence workforce planning, talent location strategy, and long-term hiring investments while balancing speed, quality, diversity, and cost.
* TEAM LEADERSHIP & CAPABILITY BUILDING: Builds and leads a high-performing, regionally distributed recruiting team, setting clear expectations, developing capabilities, and driving accountability, inclusion, engagement, and continuous improvement. Creates an environment that fosters strong business acumen, consultative partnership, and operational excellence.
* GLOBAL HIRING DELIVERY & PERFORMANCE: Leads end-to-end professional hiring delivery across NA, ensuring consistent execution, service level accountability, strong stakeholder relationships, and high-quality hiring outcomes through performance monitoring, data-driven decision making, and continuous course correction.
* TALENT PIPELINE & SOURCING STRATEGY: Defines and leads proactive sourcing, pipelining, and talent attraction strategies to build strong and diverse talent pipelines that meet current and future hiring demand. Develops innovative approaches to address critical skill gaps and long-term workforce requirements.
* BUSINESS PARTNERSHIP & WORKFORCE INSIGHTS: Serves as a trusted strategic partner to senior business and HR leaders across NA, providing labor market intelligence, workforce insights, and recruiting analytics to inform workforce planning, hiring strategies, and organizational decisions. Proactively identifies talent risks and opportunities and influences hiring strategies through strong consultative relationships and executive presence.
* EMPLOYER BRAND & CANDIDATE EXPERIENCE: Partners to enhance employer brand and deliver a consistent, high-quality candidate experience, improving attraction, engagement, and conversion outcomes across the region with an emphasis on local talent attraction levers.
* VENDOR & CHANNEL PERFORMANCE PARTNERSHIP: Partners on vendor and channel strategy, monitoring performance and optimizing external solutions to drive value and continuous improvement.
* COMPLIANCE & RISK MANAGEMENT: Ensures recruiting practices meet legal, regulatory, and organizational standards across NA, partnering across functions to mitigate risk, maintain compliant hiring practices, and navigate country-specific employment considerations.
* FUTURE TALENT & STRATEGIC WORKFORCE INITIATIVES: Leads or partners on strategic talent initiatives that strengthen the organization's future workforce capabilities, including early career programs, emerging talent strategies, workforce planning initiatives, organizational growth priorities, and talent-related aspects of mergers, acquisitions, integrations, and business transformation efforts.

**Qualifications**
------------------

Minimum Qualifications

* Minimum of six years of related work experience, including three years of supervisory experience.
* Demonstrated success leading talent acquisition strategy and recruiting operations across NA, with deep understanding of regional labor markets, talent landscapes, workforce trends, and hiring practices.
* Demonstrated success building trusted partnerships with senior business leaders and HR leadership and influencing workforce, organizational, and talent decisions within a complex global organization.
* Experience leading geographically distributed recruiting teams and delivering results across diverse cultural, business, and regulatory environments.
* Confirmed experience with recruiting technology, digital tools, analytics, and performance metrics.
* Ability to influence and collaborate effectively with stakeholders across NA and global teams.

Preferred Qualifications

* Excellent communication, relationship-building, and interpersonal skills, with the ability to effectively engage and influence candidates, hiring managers, senior leaders, and key stakeholders across NA and diverse market environments.
* Experience designing, leading, or scaling Early Career, Graduate, Internship, Apprenticeship, or Emerging Talent programs across multiple countries and markets.
* Experience supporting mergers, acquisitions, divestitures, workforce integrations, or large-scale organizational transformation initiatives.
* Strong executive presence and ability to influence senior stakeholders through data, market intelligence, and talent expertise.
* Commitment to diversity, equity, and inclusion in recruitment practices.
* Ability to thrive in a fast-paced, dynamic, global environment and adapt quickly to changing priorities.
* Adept at leveraging data to drive KPIs and metrics, monitor performance, develop action plans, and tell a clear story through data.

**Additional Information**
--------------------------

The expected salary for this position is $165,000 - $200,000. Compensation varies depending on a wide array of factors including but not limited to the specific location, certifications, education, and level of experience. The disclosed range estimate may be adjusted for any applicable geographic differential associated with the location at which the position may be filled. This position is eligible for a discretionary incentive award. The incentive award amount is dependent upon company performance and your personal performance. At Cargill we put people first. As part of your overall rewards, we offer a comprehensive benefit program including medical and/or other benefits dependent on the position offered and hours worked. Visit: https://www.cargill.com/page/my-health/mh-health-and-wellness to learn more (subject to certain collective bargaining agreements for Union positions).

Equal Opportunity Employer, including Disability/Vet.

*At Cargill, we care about your safety and want your job search experience to be a positive one. Unfortunately, there are scams out there where individuals pretend to be Cargill recruiters to try to collect personal information or request payment. Please know that Cargill will* ***never*** *ask you for money during the hiring process, and in most cases, we only accept applications through our official* *careers site**, with the exception of some roles in our production plants. If something doesn't feel right or you have questions, don't hesitate to* *contact us**. To learn more, visit our* *Notice on Fraudulent Job Offers**.*

card.title: Plant Manager
card.description:
**Company Description**

At **Link Snacks**, we show up hungry, roll up our sleeves, plaid or otherwise, and dive straight into the hard work. We don’t hide from challenges; we hunt them down. We push harder, move faster, and take the kinds of big swings that built this business in the North Woods of Wisconsin four decades ago.

We’re everyday people who deliver extraordinary results. Innovation, creativity, and urgency aren’t buzzwords, they’re expectations. And just like the real protein snacks we make across our global house of brands—Jack Link’s®*,* Lorissa’s Kitchen®*,* Golden Island®*,* BiFi®*, and* Peperami® *and* KOOEE!® to name a few—there’s nothing artificial about us. What you see is exactly what you get: humble, gritty, passionate people who show up every day ready to not just be a participate in the meat snack industry that the Link Family created, but to move faster, innovate harder and keep raising the bar so high, the rest of the world needs a ladder just to see it.

Dominating this space across the world takes a team. A team that runs together, succeeds together, and celebrates together. A team that’s full of relentless energy and spirit that can only be fueled by one thing: a fist full of our delicious meat snacks.

Real Meat Protein. Real People. Real Results. THAT is Link Snacks.

 **Job Description**

The Plant Manager directs overall plant operations and the retail store ensuring the achievement of production objectives at the lowest cost consistent with the company quality standards and customer delivery requirements.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

This list of duties and responsibilities is not all-inclusive and may be expanded to include other duties and responsibilities, as management may deem necessary from time to time.

1. Prioritize, schedule and delegate work assignments and directly supervise the plant staff to ensure the achievement of production objectives at the lowest cost consistent with company quality requirements.

2. Monitor suppliers to ensure that they efficiently and effectively provide needed goods or services within budgetary limits.

3. Direct or coordinate financial or budget activities to fund operations, maximize investments, or increase efficiency.

4. Evaluate, recommend, and implement improvements in methods and processes to increase productivity and quality.

5. Develop plans for the maximum utilization of materials, machines and employees.

6. Review production costs and product quality; modify production and inventory control programs to maintain and enhance profitable operation of division.

7. Ensure proper maintenance of equipment and building and establish plant housekeeping standards.

8. Develop and recommend plant capital and operating budgets to ensure conformance to budgets.

9. Develop policies and procedures to ensure compliance with OSHA, environmental and various regulatory agencies.

10. Enforce safety and work rules and company housekeeping standards.

11. Recommend locations for new facilities or oversee the remodeling or renovating of current facilities.

12. Ensure compliance with all quality, SQF, HACCP, safety, and sanitation regulations.

Supervisory Responsibilities

Manage supervisors who supervise employees in the manufacturing of company products. Is responsible for the overall direction, coordination, and evaluation of this unit. Carry out supervisory responsibilities in accordance with the organization's policies and applicable laws. Responsibilities include planning, assigning, and directing work; appraising performance; rewarding and disciplining employees; addressing complaints and resolving problems.

 **Qualifications**

To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

Education and/or Experience

Requires a bachelor's degree in production and operations management from a four-year college or university plus a minimum of five years progressively responsible related experience; or ten years progressively responsible related experience; or a combination of education and experience. Requires the ability to operate a computer and

standard office machines. Requires a general knowledge of company products and procedures. Requires a working knowledge of accounting methods and cost control procedures.

Language Skills

Ability to read, analyze, and interpret blueprints, customer specifications, general business periodicals, technical procedures, or governmental regulations. Ability to write reports and business correspondence. Ability to effectively present information and respond to questions from managers, customers, and other employees of the organization.

Mathematical Skills

Ability to work with mathematical concepts such as probability and statistical inference. Ability to apply concepts such as algebraic formulas, fractions, percentages, ratios, and proportions to practical situations.

Reasoning Ability

Ability to define problems, collect data, establish facts, and draw valid conclusions. Ability to interpret an extensive variety of technical instructions in mathematical or diagram form and deal with several abstract and concrete variables.

Physical Demands

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

Wear required safety equipment when on shop floor. While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to talk or hear. The employee frequently is required to stand. The employee is occasionally required to walk; sit; and use hands to finger, handle, or touch objects, tools, or controls. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision.

Work Environment

The work environment characteristics described here are representative of those an employee encounters while performing the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions. While performing the duties of this job, the employee is occasionally exposed to fumes or airborne particles. The noise level in the work environment is usually moderate to loud.

 **Additional Information**

*The hiring range for this role is $135,000 - $145,000 yearly**. Actual wages will vary based on several factors, including but not limited to external market data, internal equity, location, and candidate skill set and experience. Base pay is just one component of Jack Link’s Total Rewards package for Team Members. Other rewards may include annual incentive and program-specific awards. Jack Link’s provides a variety of benefits to eligible Team Members, including medical, dental and vision benefits, life and disability insurance, 401k participation, paid holidays, and paid time off.*

**PHYSICAL DEMANDS**: 
The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to be successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

While performing the duties of this job the employee is regularly required to stand, walk, use hands to finger, handle, or feel, lift and/or move up to 25 pounds, and talk or hear. The employee is occasionally required to sit, and reach with hands and arms. The employee must occasionally lift and/or move up to 50 pounds. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision.

**WORK ENVIRONMENT**: 
The work environment characteristics described here are representative of those an employee encounters while performing the essential functions of this job. The work environment is a plant / office setting with varying degrees of temperatures and noise levels. Exposure to manufacturing equipment movement and wet / slippery floors. Travel may be required.

**EQUAL EMPLOYMENT OPPORTUNITY EMPLOYER:** 
Jack Link’s provides equal employment opportunity (EEO) to all persons regardless of age, color, national origin, citizenship status, physical or mental disability, race, religion, creed, gender, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity and/or expression, genetic information, marital status, status with regard to public assistance, veteran status, or any other characteristic that is protected by federal, state or local law.

**E-VERIFY:** 
Jack Link’s is participant in the federal E-Verify program to confirm the identity and employment authorization of all newly hired employees. For information about the E-Verify program, please visit: http://www.uscis.gov/e-verify/employees

card.title: Senior Manager, Manufacturing Engineering
card.description:
******Relocation assistance is available for this position.******
**Who We Are**
Stored Energy Systems (SENS) is an award-winning manufacturer of premium quality power conversion products located in Longmont, CO. In business for over 50 years, SENS is the market leader with a proven track record of providing highly reliable battery chargers, DC power systems, and related products to industrial markets. For more information on our company please see our web site at www.sens-usa.com .
 
 
**View the SENS Product Catalog**
**Summary**
SENS is seeking a manufacturing engineering leader to help build and scale the organization, processes, and technical capabilities required for our next stage of growth. Supporting the expansion of existing manufacturing operations and establishing new operations at our Broomfield Systems manufacturing factory, this leader will establish the manufacturing engineering strategy, develop a multidisciplinary team, and translate business growth plans into manufacturing capacity and reliable production processes for our fastest-growing products.
 
 
This role leads manufacturing engineering, industrialization, tooling, test systems, automation, and technical production support for our systems products, with a strong emphasis on configure-to-order assembly manufacturing. Working closely with Production, Design Engineering, Quality, Safety, and Supply Chain, the Senior Manager will establish clear priorities, strengthen new product and production transfer readiness, and deliver measurable improvements in productivity, quality, cost, and equipment reliability.
 
 
A successful candidate will combine organizational leadership with practical technical judgment, building a team that can support daily production while executing the improvements and investments needed to scale.
 
 
**Responsibilities**

* Help to build and develop the manufacturing engineering organization. Assess current capabilities, define the team structure and staffing plan, recruit talent, and develop engineers and technical leaders to support SENS’s growth.
* Establish performance measures and execution discipline. Set departmental goals, review project and operational performance, communicate risks and resource needs, and hold the team accountable for measurable improvements in manufacturing readiness, capacity, productivity, and equipment reliability.
* Establish and execute the manufacturing engineering roadmap. Translate business growth, product plans, and production requirements into prioritized initiatives for manufacturing capacity, processes, tooling, test systems, automation, and equipment reliability.
* Lead manufacturing readiness for new products and production transfers. Partner with Design Engineering, Production, Quality, and Planning & Fulfillment to establish readiness criteria and ensure processes, equipment, tooling, test capability, documentation, and training are in place before production release.
* Develop scalable manufacturing processes and standards. Establish consistent methods for process development, validation, work instructions, engineering changes, and production controls across manufacturing locations while accommodating product-specific requirements.
* Expand manufacturing capacity and improve productivity. Lead engineering efforts in capacity analysis, line balancing, factory layout, workflow, cycle-time reduction, and constraint elimination to support production demand and improve labor efficiency.
* Provide reliable technical support to Production. Establish clear support coverage, escalation processes, and problem-solving practices that resolve production issues promptly and prevent recurrence while maintaining progress on strategic projects.
* Guide manufacturing technology development. Lead technical specialists responsible for manufacturing test systems, production software, tooling, and automation. Prioritize investments based on safety, quality, capacity, reliability, and financial return.
* Improve production equipment reliability. Establish equipment ownership, maintenance strategies, critical spare requirements, and preventive and predictive maintenance practices in partnership with Production and technical support teams.
* Manage projects, capital investments, and departmental resources. Develop business cases, budgets, schedules, and resource plans; oversee implementation and production acceptance; and verify that projects deliver their expected operational and financial benefits.
* Partner with Design Engineering on manufacturability. Incorporate manufacturing feedback early in product development and engineering changes to improve assembly, testability, quality, serviceability, and cost.
* Drive safe processes and sustained quality improvement. Partner with EHS and Quality to incorporate risk assessment, error prevention, root cause analysis, and corrective action into manufacturing processes and equipment changes.
* Oversee the development and maintenance of manufacturing processes, work instructions, test procedures, tooling, fixtures, automation systems, and production software solutions.
* Be directly accountable for engineering project delivery, manufacturing readiness, equipment reliability, and validated improvement benefits, while sharing accountability with Production and Quality for labor efficiency and first-pass yield (FPY).

**Required Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s degree in Engineering or a related technical discipline, or an additional 4 tears of manufacturing engineering experience.
* Eight or more years of experience in manufacturing engineering, production engineering, industrialization, or a related technical manufacturing role.
* Three or more years of experience directly leading engineering or technical teams, including setting priorities, developing employees, allocating resources, and managing performance.
* Demonstrated success improving manufacturing performance, with measurable results in productivity, capacity, quality, cost, or equipment reliability.
* Experience developing and improving manufacturing processes, tooling, fixtures, work instructions, and production controls, including introducing new or revised products into production.
* Ability to lead engineers and technical specialists across manufacturing processes, test systems, automation, and production support, using sound technical judgment to evaluate solutions and resolve issues.
* Practical application of Lean Manufacturing and structured problem-solving methods, including root cause analysis and corrective action.
* Experience leading cross-functional projects with Production, Design Engineering, Quality, Safety, and Supply Chain, balancing daily production needs with longer-term improvement priorities.
* Experience planning and executing manufacturing improvement or capital equipment projects, including defining scope, schedules, resource requirements, and expected business results.
* Strong communication and organizational skills, with the ability to translate business objectives into clear team priorities and communicate progress, risks, and decisions.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Experience in manufacturing of configure-to-order (CTO) and engineered-to-order (ETO) electrical systems such as switchgear, switchboard, etc.
* Experience with manufacturing software development, automated test systems, and data acquisition platforms.
* Experience using ERP systems such as SyteLine for BOM management, item masters, engineering changes, and manufacturing planning.
* Lean Six Sigma Green Belt, Black Belt, or equivalent certification.
* Experience managing departmental budgets and capital equipment projects from business case through production acceptance.

**Location:**
Longmont, CO
 
 
**Base Compensation:**
$120,000 - $175,000 is the projected annual base salary range for this role and will be determined on the candidate’s overall qualifications and experience.
 
 
****Bonus:**
This position is eligible for an annual bonus based on individual and company performance.**
**Closing Date:**
December 15th. While we expect to keep the position open through this date, the posting may be extended or closed early based on applicant volume and hiring needs.
 
 
**Onsite Perks**

* Free gym with 24/7 access
* Free Electric Vehicle charging
* Breakfast and Lunch Café
* After hours Grab & Go snacks
* Basketball court
* Walking paths

**Benefits**

* Paid Time Off
* Paid holidays
* Medical insurance
* Dental insurance
* Vision insurance
* Short-term and long-term disability
* Life insurance
* 401(k) plan with immediate vesting
* Employee referral program
* Tuition reimbursement
* Professional development

At SENS, our culture is rooted in a set of core values that reflect who we are and how we work. In a recent 2025 poll, our employees identified the values that best define us: “Innovative”, “Respectful”, “Inviting”, “Flexible”, “Collaborative”, and “Growth Driven”. Our team describes us as a dynamic, forward-thinking company where everyone has the opportunity to thrive.
 
 
We pride ourselves on being an equal opportunity employer, fully dedicated to fostering inclusion and diversity. We welcome all applicants, regardless of race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, genetic information, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, or any other legally protected characteristic.
 
 
We hope you're interested in making a difference with us. Even if you don't feel that you meet every qualification listed in this job description, we still encourage you to apply.

card.description:
**Position Description:**

* The Plant Manager is responsible for assisting the Director of Plant Services in engineering, custodial, and minor maintenance at selected facilities as assigned by the Director of Plant Services by starting, stopping, and observing all equipment that is interconnected with the air conditioning and/or heating system, safety, security, cleanliness, and the entire appearance at various facilities.
* The position can require extend or on call work hours due to emergencies or extenuating circumstances related to safety or operational routine.

**Scope of Responsibility:**

* Opens building in morning; secures building in afternoon.
* Operates heating and air conditioning systems.
* Sees that rooms are properly ventilated.
* Replaces light globes or fluorescent tubes.
* Receives supplies, checks inventory requesting janitorial supplies; supplies custodial staff. Do not supply to cafeteria or stadium.
* Reports vandalism immediately to principal and keeps reports.
* Checks firefighting equipment and playground equipment for good functioning and safety.
* Repairs, removes or secures any unsafe equipment, reports same to principal.
* Cuts and maintains school yard and shrubs, watering regularly.
* Removes trash and debris from premises.
* Buffs floor when appropriate.
* Maintains cleanliness of halls and entrances during the day.
* Cleans classroom units as specified in accordance with work schedule and specified school needs.
* Is available for school and school sponsored activities. Outside agencies will pay for use of building as prescribed in policy manual.
* Sets up for assemblies, conferences, plays, programs when required.
* Supervises custodial staff, inspects their work, assigns duties, keeps and reports the time for himself/ herself and personnel, etc. in coordination with principal.
* Light maintenance functions, makes minor repairs such as replacing faucet handles, light switches, door knobs and door adjustments, glass repairs, painting, etc. for all buildings on school plant.
* Responsible to carry and answers system issued iPhone before, during and after normal work hours due to emergencies or extenuating circumstances related to safety or operational routine.
* Maintains files and operates computer and other machines.
* Performs other duties as assigned by the Director of Plant Services.

**Skills and Qualifications:**

* We seek detail-oriented, independent self-starters who demonstrate an unwavering commitment to raising student achievement and who have a record of high performance in challenging situations.
* Successful candidates will also demonstrate and/or possess:
* 3+ years of progressively increasing experience custodial services.
* Strong communication skills in multiple settings and the ability to be an engaging change agent and culture creator that can inspire and motivate.
* Exceptional analytical and problem-solving skills, with an ability to use quantitative and qualitative data to make decisions and recommendations.
* Collaborative management style, with a proven track record of working with diverse individuals at all levels to drive decision-making and results.
* Maintain a valid Louisiana drivers’ license.
* Have knowledge of driving laws, interpreting traffic signals, signs.
* Ability to operate a manual transmission.

**Desirable Qualifications:**

* High school diploma or GED/Hi Set
* Two years of experience in a mechanical trade.
* Two years of college with 48 credit hours earned.

**Physical Involvement:**

* Walking and carrying tools, equipment, building materials, etc. are constant, everyday requirements.
* Surfaces vary including mud conditions after a rain, gravel, concrete, dirt, grass, etc.
* Climbing 6, 8, 10, and 12 foot step ladder, extension ladder, stairs and scaffolding are routinely required.
* This climbing often includes carrying of tools, building materials, etc.
* Trunk flexion and squatting are necessary requirements in accomplishing tasks such as working under raised buildings, in attic spaces, toilet room enclosures, etc., again often necessitating carrying tools, building materials, etc.
* Lifting is required daily in accomplishing tasks.
* Building materials, electrical panels, small generator and pump equipment, desks, full mop buckets, etc., are necessarily moved, in some cases loaded and unloaded from vehicles.
* Fifty pounds is the maximum expected load for one person.
* Two and three person coordinated lifting is occasionally required.

**Compensation:**

* JPS offers a competitive salary that is commensurate with experience.
* JPS also offers a competitive benefits package.

**Overview**

Microsoft’s Cloud Operations & Innovation (CO+I) is the engine that powers our cloud services. As a CO+I Engineering, Procurement, & Construction (EPC) **Regional Commissioning Director,** you will perform a key role in delivering the core infrastructure and foundational technologies for Microsoft's over 200 online businesses including Bing, Office 365, Xbox, OneDrive and the Microsoft Azure platform.

Our infrastructure is comprised of a large global portfolio of more than 200 datacenters in 32 countries and millions of servers. Our foundation is built upon and managed by a team of subject matter experts working to support services for more than 1 billion customers and 20 million businesses in over 90 countries worldwide.

With environmental sustainability and optimization at the forefront of our datacenter design and operations, we continue to grow and evolve as we meet the ever-changing business demands that hold Microsoft as a world-class cloud provider.

Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond.

 **Responsibilities** 

* Lead regional commissioning strategy and execution across multiple EPC datacenter projects, managers, vendors, and delivery partners.
* Manage and develop commissioning leaders, building team capability, succession depth, performance accountability, and consistent regional operating rhythms.
* Set regional commissioning priorities, governance, standards, and delivery expectations to ensure reliable, safe, and predictable turnover to Operations.
* Drive alignment across EPC, Engineering, Construction, Operations, Security, Procurement, and vendor leadership to resolve systemic risks and accelerate delivery outcomes.

* Monitor portfolio-level commissioning metrics, schedule risks, budget impacts, readiness gaps, and escalation themes, translating insights into action plans and leadership updates.
* Champion continuous improvement across commissioning standards, procedures, reporting, safety practices, and scalable delivery models for regional and global consistency.
* Embody our culture and values.

**Required Qualifications**

* Doctorate Degree in Mechanical Engineering, Materials Engineering, Reliability Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or related field AND 5+ years technical engineering experience
 + OR Master's Degree in Mechanical Engineering, Materials Engineering, Reliability Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or related field AND 7+ years technical engineering experience
 + OR Bachelor's Degree in Mechanical Engineering, Materials Engineering, Reliability Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or related field AND 8+ years technical engineering experience.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Doctorate Degree in Mechanical Engineering, Materials Engineering, Reliability Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or related field AND 7+ years technical engineering experience

* 4+ years people management experience.

Join Kite, as we make even bigger advances in cancer therapies, and help shape where our business and medical science goes next.

Join Kite and help create more tomorrows.

**Job Description**
-------------------

We are seeking a highly motivated individual to join our team as Director, Supplier Quality to be the Compliance and Technical Lead for the global quality network of Supplier Quality Management. This role will report to the Sr. Director, External and Supplier Quality. Key responsibilities include overseeing all Quality aspects associated with global suppliers and vendors while acting as a point of contact for compliance and technical issues.

**Responsibilities:**

* Serves as the Quality lead for Company’s global suppliers and vendors.
* Develop and lead the global Supplier Quality Management (SQM) strategy, governance model, procedures, and operating standards.
* Define supplier segmentation and oversight requirements based on GMP criticality, material/service risk, patient impact, and supply-chain risk.

* Monitor CAPA effectiveness and recurring supplier issues.
* Lead risk assessments for changes in supplier status, manufacturing location, process, specifications, ownership, regulatory status, or business continuity.
* Evaluate quality risks associated with single-source materials, long lead-time materials, critical raw materials, and constrained suppliers.
* Partner with Supply Chain and Technical Operations to balance GMP compliance, patient safety, product quality, and supply continuity when supplier risks emerge
* Ensure audit observations are appropriately classified, investigated, responded to, and closed.
* Maintain the supplier quality system in a continuous state of inspection readiness.
* Lead escalation for chronic supplier performance problems and determine when additional controls, suspension, or disqualification are appropriate.

* Bachelor’s Degree and 12+ years’ experience of Compliance and Quality Assurance/Quality Control within Biopharmaceutical or Pharmaceutical manufacturing, OR
High School Degree and 16+ years’ experience of Compliance and Quality Assurance/Quality Control within Biopharmaceutical or Pharmaceutical manufacturing 

**Preferred Qualifications:**

* Advanced science degree.
* Deep knowledge and experience in quality assurance in a highly regulated manufacturing environment.
* Well versed in Compliance, Auditing, Validation, and testing of biopharmaceuticals, preferred.
* Working knowledge of Quality Systems
* Working knowledge of current regulatory requirements (FDA/EMA, JP)
* Minimum 6 years of Compliance/QA and/or QC lab management experience in the biotech and/or pharmaceutical industry
* Strong knowledge of current GMP, SOPs and quality control processes
* Identifying, writing evaluating and closing OOS’s and investigations
* Strong knowledge or ability to understand/interpret manufacturing processes
* Process/Equipment/laboratory instrument IQ/OQ/PQ/PV
* Prior people management experience.
* Proficient in MS Word, Excel, Power Point and other applications
* Ability to communicate effectively (written, verbal) and work independently with scientific/technical personnel.
* Comfortable in a fast-paced company environment with minimal direction and able to adjust workload based upon changing priorities
* Self-motivated, detail-oriented, and willing to accept temporary responsibilities outside of initial job description
* Ability to think critically and demonstrate troubleshooting and problem-solving skills
* Ability to exercise judgement and take appropriate action where precedent may not exist
Excellent interpersonal, verbal, written and presentation communication skills 

 

**People Leader Accountabilities:**

* Create Inclusion - knowing the business value of diverse teams, modeling inclusion, and embedding the value of diversity in the way they manage their teams.
* Develop Talent - understand the skills, experience, aspirations and potential of their employees and coach them on current performance and future potential. They ensure employees are receiving the feedback and insight needed to grow, develop and realize their purpose.
Empower Teams - connect the team to the organization by aligning goals, purpose, and organizational objectives, and holding them to account. They provide the support needed to remove barriers and connect their team to the broader ecosystem.

card.description:
As an employee of Boehringer Ingelheim, you will actively contribute to the discovery, development, and delivery of our products to our patients and customers. Our global presence provides an opportunity for all employees to collaborate internationally, offering visibility and the opportunity to directly contribute to the company's success. We realize that our strength and competitive advantage lie with our people. We support our employees in several ways to foster a healthy working environment, meaningful work, mobility, networking, and work-life balance. Our competitive compensation and benefit programs reflect Boehringer Ingelheim's high regard for our employees.
 
 
The head, Data & AI Governance, Quality & Assurance is accountable for data & AI trust, quality, transparency, compliance, and responsible use across data products, AI products, analytical assets, and agents within the U.S. organization. The role owns U.S. governance frameworks, controls, quality and assurance standards, stewardship expectations, and independent oversight across the lifecycle, aligned with applicable global policies and standards.
 
 
The Data & AI Governance, Quality & Assurance sets acceptance criteria, identifies and escalates material risks, provides evidence for accountable decisions, and drives adoption of AI and agentic workflows to modernize data and AI governance, quality, and assurance across the U.S. organization.

 

This role is based on-site at our Ridgefield, CT location with hybrid flexibility of 2-3 days per week on-site.

**Duties & Responsibilities**
-----------------------------

* Owns the U.S. Data & AI governance and assurance framework, aligned with global policies and standards.
* Defines policies, standards, controls, and accountability structures.
* Sets data quality, stewardship, observability, and assurance expectations.
* Governs metadata, catalog, lineage, access, permitted use, and information-management policy.
* Governs KPI, business-rule, ontology, semantic, and AI or agent registration processes.
* Defines responsible AI controls and independent validation criteria.
* Provides independent lifecycle oversight and risk-acceptance recommendations.
* Builds governance, quality, stewardship, and assurance capability.
* Drives adoption of AI and agentic workflows to modernize data and AI governance, quality, stewardship, and assurance processes.

**Requirements**
----------------

* Bachelor’s degree in Information Management, Data Science, Computer Science, Law, Risk, Quality, Business, Life Sciences, or a related field required.
* MSc, MBA, JD, or relevant graduate degree; governance, risk, audit, quality, privacy, security, or responsible AI credentials are advantageous preferred.
* Twelve-plus (12+) years of relevant experience, including senior leadership in governance, risk, compliance, quality, assurance, or information management within a complex U.S. organization.
* Demonstrated success establishing governance frameworks, decision rights, controls, stewardship models, and independent assurance across complex organizations.
* Deep knowledge of data quality, metadata, lineage, catalogs, access, permitted use, observability, issue management, and control evidence.
* Strong understanding of responsible AI, model and agent governance, lifecycle controls, registration, validation, monitoring, and release assurance.
* Demonstrated success redesigning governance and quality processes and driving adoption of AI and agentic workflows, with measurable improvements in effectiveness, efficiency, transparency, and user experience.
* Ability to maintain independence from remediation while providing practical findings, thresholds, and risk recommendations.
* Strong analytical judgment, executive communication, regulatory influence, and escalation capability.
* Ability to lead through a matrix, align control functions and delivery teams, and build governance and stewardship capability.
* Experience in pharmaceutical, life-sciences, healthcare, or another highly regulated environment.
 

**Eligibility Requirements** :

* Must be legally authorized to work in the United States without restriction.
* Must be willing to take a drug test and post-offer physical (if required).
* Must be 18 years of age or older.

card.title: APP Medical Director, Quality & Safety
card.description:
**Help shape the clinical future of one of the region's most respected healthcare organizations.**

Yale New Haven Health Urgent Care is seeking an experienced Advanced Practice Provider leader to serve as **APP Medical Director, Quality & Safety**.

The Medical Director reports to the Chief Medical Officer and provides direct leadership to an assigned group of providers and Lead Providers, while holding network-wide responsibility for clinical quality standards, quality surveillance, patient safety, and performance improvement across Yale New Haven Health Urgent Care. This senior leadership position combines meaningful clinical practice with the opportunity to advance evidence-based care and strengthen clinical performance across a growing network in Connecticut and New York.

**Why Join Yale New Haven Health Urgent Care?**

* Regional leadership opportunity with impact across urgent care centers throughout Connecticut and New York.
* Partnership with an experienced and collaborative medical leadership team.
* Ability to influence clinical quality, safety, and provider performance at scale.
* Opportunity to mentor providers and develop future clinical leaders.
* Strong operational infrastructure and organizational support.
* Continued clinical practice while serving in a senior leadership role.
* Proudly affiliated with Yale New Haven Health.

**A Regional Leadership Opportunity**

Working collaboratively with the Chief Medical Officer, fellow Medical Directors, Lead Providers, and operational leaders, the APP Medical Director, Quality & Safety will translate clinical performance data, quality findings, and emerging risks into meaningful improvements in care delivery, provider performance, and patient outcomes.

**What You'll Do**

* Provide direct leadership, performance management, coaching, and professional development for an assigned group of Advanced Practice Providers.
* Directly supervise and develop assigned Lead Providers, supporting their effectiveness in provider oversight, clinical escalation, and quality improvement.
* Lead network-wide clinical quality and patient safety initiatives, including quality surveillance, clinical event review, clinical risk identification, and performance improvement.

* Establish and oversee chart review, documentation integrity, coding accuracy, and provider feedback processes, ensuring findings translate into appropriate corrective actions and measurable improvements in clinical care.

* Develop and monitor evidence-based clinical standards, including diagnostic testing, clinically significant results follow-up, referral and escalation processes, and adherence to established clinical protocols.

* Partner with the Chief Medical Officer and operational leadership on clinical governance, regulatory readiness, and risk mitigation.

* Maintain meaningful clinical practice while serving in a leadership capacity.

**What Success Looks Like**

A successful leader in this role will:

* Demonstrate measurable improvements in clinical quality, patient safety, and provider performance across the urgent care network.

* Develop and support high-performing providers and Lead Providers through effective coaching, accountability, and professional development.

* Use clinical performance data, chart review findings, and quality metrics to identify opportunities, implement improvements, and sustain results.

* Foster consistent, evidence-based care and a culture of collaboration, accountability, and continuous improvement across geographically diverse teams.

* Champion a patient-centered approach to urgent care that supports timely access, appropriate clinical management, and seamless coordination across the Yale New Haven Health delivery network.

**Qualifications**

* Current unrestricted PA or APRN licensure and appropriate board certification.
* Significant urgent care clinical experience with expertise managing the broad range of acute illnesses, injuries, and procedures encountered in urgent care practice.
* Substantial clinical leadership experience, including direct provider supervision, performance management, accountability for clinical quality and patient safety outcomes, and successful implementation of measurable clinical improvement initiatives.
* Strong collaboration and relationship-building skills across multidisciplinary teams.
* Experience leading across multiple clinical sites and utilizing quality and performance data to drive improvement strongly preferred.
* Ability to travel throughout the region as needed to support providers, quality initiatives, and operational priorities.

**Working Arrangement**

* This is a regional, multi-site leadership position supporting Yale New Haven Health Urgent Care locations throughout Connecticut and New York. The position is not assigned to a single clinical site and requires travel throughout the network.
* Clinical Commitment: 0.3 FTE.
* Medical Leadership Responsibilities: 0.7 FTE.

**Ready to Take the Next Step?**

If you're an accomplished Advanced Practice Provider with a passion for clinical leadership, quality improvement, and patient safety, we invite you to explore this opportunity to make a meaningful impact across the Yale New Haven Health Urgent Care network.

**Apply today to learn more.**

card.title: Senior Director, Strategic Operations for the Center on Reinventing Public Education
card.description:
**Job Profile:**

Administrative Operations Manager 3

**Job Family:**

Administrative Operations

**Time Type:**

Full time

**Apply before 11:59 PM Arizona time the day before the posted End Date.**

**Minimum Qualifications:**

Bachelor's degree and seven (7) years of experience appropriate to the area of assignment/field including two (2) years managerial experience; OR, Any equivalent combination of experience and/or training from which comparable knowledge, skills and abilities have been achieved.
 
 
Job Profile Summary:
 
Administers and evaluates business and administrative matters within one department , including budget, operations, and programs and personnel administration.

**Job Description:**

**Salary Range** : $130,000 - $150,000 per year; offer dependent upon experience

 

The Center on Reinventing Public Education (CRPE), a leading source of transformative, evidence-based ideas about public education throughout the U.S., is seeking an experienced, strategic, creative, and detail-oriented systems thinker to serve as its Senior Director of Strategic Operations.

As a core member of the leadership team, the Senior Director will shape and lead the systems, processes, and operational strategies that enable CRPE to accelerate its national impact and internal effectiveness. This person will thoughtfully leverage AI, cross-functional collaboration, and relationships across Arizona State University to ensure CRPE operates and deploys talent most effectively as research, technology, and the education contexts change.

The Senior Director will oversee the strategy and execution of CRPE’s core organizational operations, including talent management, grant management, AI integration and adoption, and special projects. Working closely with the Center’s leaders, the Senior Director will ensure that organizational systems, policies, and practices support CRPE’s strategic priorities and reflect its commitment to a strong, inclusive staff culture. This role combines high-level strategic thinking and organizational design with hands-on implementation and problem-solving, designing systems and building the team that runs them.

The Senior Director will supervise a team of three and collaborate closely with other department leaders. CRPE is a remote team and is an especially strong fit for professionals who enjoy building effective systems, navigating complexity, and contributing to a fast-paced, high-impact organization.

**About CRPE**

The Center on Reinventing Public Education (CRPE) is a research organization at Arizona State University’s Mary Lou Fulton College for Teaching and Learning Innovation, where transformative ideas are rigorously examined and tested, and research informs action. Since 1993, we have remained independent of any single ideology while holding firmly to our core belief that public education is a goal—to prepare every child for citizenship, economic independence, and personal fulfillment—and not a particular set of institutions.

From that foundation, we study what it will take for public education to meet every student’s needs and use those insights to inform meaningful changes in policy and practice.

Our current research explores four broad topics:

* **Students and Families** : We work to understand what students and families need from their education system—and how schools can rise to meet those needs.

* **Systems:** We examine the inner workings of schools, districts, and state governments, delivering insights into how our education systems work to meet the needs of students, families, and communities.

* **Innovations:** We identify promising initiatives outside the traditional education system that have the potential to radically improve teaching and learning, including artificial intelligence, new teacher staffing models, and district-wide innovations.

* **Politics of Change:** We study the critical role of politics in determining whether school systems deliver on their promise, and explore the ways public officials, school system leaders, and change-makers can factor political thinking into their strategies for improving education.

By partnering with the Mary Lou Fulton College, we are uniquely positioned to produce evidence and ideas that lead the country toward an education system that meets the needs of every student. Over the next five years, CRPE will produce ideas and evidence that inform effective state improvement, thoughtful AI policy and implementation, and innovative approaches to ensure every learner is prepared for a boundless future.

 

**Essential Duties:**

*Organizational strategy and change leadership*

* Partner with the CRPE’s Director and Managing Director to lead the organization strategically, helping CRPE adapt its organizational model, structure, and operations as strategy evolves.
* Translate strategy into implementation, turning priorities into operating plans with clear owners, timelines, and follow-through, and keeping leadership informed through coherent internal communications.
Own organization-wide staffing plans, capacity planning, and project resourcing in partnership with research leaders. 

*AI operational leadership*

* In collaboration with CRPE’s Research Principals, adapt roles, workflows, and tools for the age of AI, bringing in new technology where it improves research and operations.
* Lead AI integration across the organization, including policy and guidance, staff training and office hours, playbooks, piloting and scaling new uses, and building staff buy-in and tracking adoption.
Ensure staff have the systems, software, and equipment they need, and that data integrity, security, and records retention protocols are in place to adhere with University guidelines. 

*Talent strategy and people operations*

* Develop and implement a strategy to attract, retain, develop, and promote talent and support an inclusive workforce, drawing on a flexible mix of full-time staff, part-time staff, interns, and contractors.
* Lead CRPE’s annual performance review cycles, aligned with university requirements.
* Lead culture initiatives, including all-staff meetings, the annual staff retreat, professional development, and supporting staff and supervisors through feedback, to build a positive, respectful culture.
Supervise, coach, and develop a team of three: the People and Operations Manager, the Project Coordinator, and the Grants Manager. 

*University partnership manager*

* Serve as CRPE’s lead liaison and negotiator with ASU department leads, including HR, finance, sponsored projects, and IT partners. Find solutions within university systems and advocate effectively for CRPE’s needs.
Build collaborative relationships with other ASU colleges and units that advance CRPE’s mission. 

*Financial strategy and oversight*

Supervise and partner with the Grants Manager to oversee CRPE’s long-range financial strategy, including annual spending plans, multi-year forecasts, and funding and runway planning. 



*Oversight of special projects*

Lead or sponsor cross-functional projects and strategic initiatives that vary in complexity, urgency, and frequency as needs arise. 

 

**Desired Qualifications:**

* Master's degree in business, public administration, or a related field preferred.
* AI fluency and change leadership. Hands-on proficiency with generative AI tools and demonstrated experience leading organizational adoption of new technology, including developing policy, training staff, and building buy-in across teams with varied comfort levels.
* Talent and performance management. Experience designing and running recruitment, including coaching supervisors and managing contractor relationships.
* Complex project management. Experience leading multiple concurrent, cross-functional projects to completion amid shifting priorities and tight timelines. A track record of diagnosing operational challenges and building better systems.
Operations management. Experience overseeing financial and operational systems, including budget management and forecasting, grants administration, and human resources, in a nonprofit, education, or university setting (preferred). 

 

**Working Environment:**

* Activities are performed in an environmentally controlled office setting and involve extended periods of sitting, keyboarding, and use of a computer mouse.
* Position may require travel between campus locations or buildings for meetings or job-related tasks.
* Regular activities require the ability to manage and adjust to changing priorities, including handling time-sensitive tasks and resolving conflicts.
* MLFC supports flexible work options for certain positions, such as alternate work schedules and hybrid or full remote arrangements, subject to approvals per ASU policy.

**Department Statement:**

ASU’s Mary Lou Fulton College for Teaching and Learning Innovation creates knowledge, mobilizes people, and takes action to improve education. Nationally recognized as a leader in teacher preparation, leadership development and scholarly research, Mary Lou Fulton College for Teaching and Learning Innovation prepares over 8,000 educators annually. MLFC faculty create knowledge by drawing from a wide range of academic disciplines to gain insight into important questions about the process of learning, the practice of teaching and the effects of education policy. MLFC mobilizes people through bachelor's, master's and doctoral degree programs, through non-degree professional development programs and through socially embedded, multilateral community engagement. MLFC takes action by bringing people and ideas together to increase the capabilities of individual educators and the performance of education systems.

 

Aligned with ASU’s charter , MLFC is committed to advancing inclusive excellence in our curricula, programming and institutional relationships.

**Driving Requirement:**

Driving is not required for this position.

**Location:**

Campus: Tempe

**Funding:**

Grant Funded 

**Instructions to Apply:**

Current employees, student workers seeking staff opportunities, and students applying for student worker positions must apply directly through the Workday Jobs Hub .

 

To be considered, your application must include all of the following attachments:

* Cover letter
Resume or CV 

 

Multiple documents may be uploaded in the attachments section. Alternatively, applicants may combine all required materials into a single PDF for submission. Please ensure uploaded documents are clearly labeled and include your name.

 

Please ensure your resume includes all employment information in month and year format, for example 6/04 to 8/14, along with job title, job duties, and employer name for each position. Your resume should clearly demonstrate how your experience and background meet the minimum and desired qualifications for this position. Incomplete applications or missing required materials may not be considered.

 

**Important:** Do not withdraw your application to make edits. Once an application is withdrawn, it cannot be edited, reactivated, or replaced with a new submission. If you have questions or need assistance, please contact The Office of Human Resources Talent Acquisition before the posting close date.

 

Graduate Assistant, Intern and part-time positions are counted as half time for experience equivalency, meaning one year equals six months of experience.

 

Only electronic applications will be accepted for this position. By submitting an application, you confirm that the information provided is accurate and complete.

 

**ASU Statement:**

Arizona State University is a new model for American higher education, an unprecedented combination of academic excellence, entrepreneurial energy and broad access. This New American University is a single, unified institution comprising four differentiated campuses positively impacting the economic, social, cultural and environmental health of the communities it serves. Its research is inspired by real world application blurring the boundaries that traditionally separate academic disciplines. ASU serves more than 100,000 students in metropolitan Phoenix, Arizona, the nation's fifth largest city. ASU champions inclusive excellence, and welcomes students from all fifty states and more than one hundred nations across the globe.

 

ASU is a tobacco-free university. For details visit https://wellness.asu.edu/explore-wellness/body/alcohol-and-drugs/tobacco

 

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, protected veteran status, or any other basis protected by law.

 

**Notice of Availability of the ASU Annual Security and Fire Safety Report:**

In compliance with federal law, ASU prepares an annual report on campus security and fire safety programs and resources. ASU’s Annual Security and Fire Safety Report is available online at https://www.asu.edu/police/PDFs/ASU-Clery-Report.pdf . You may request a hard copy of the report by contacting the ASU Police Department at 480-965-3456.

 

Relocation Assistance – For information about schools, housing child resources, neighborhoods, hospitals, community events, and taxes, visit https://cfo.asu.edu/az-resources .

 

ASU’s comprehensive benefits package is a key part of your total compensation. Visit the ASU Compensation Estimator

**Employment Verification Statement:**

ASU conducts pre-employment screening which may include verification of work history, academic credentials, licenses, and certifications.

**Background Check Statement:**

ASU conducts pre-employment screening for all positions which includes a criminal background check, verification of work history, academic credentials, licenses, and certifications. Employment is contingent upon successful passing of the background check.

**Fingerprint Check Statement:**

This position is considered safety/security sensitive and will include a fingerprint check. Employment is contingent upon successful passing of the fingerprint check.

card.description:
**Job Summary and Responsibilities**

The Director of Destination Care Operations drives the day-to-day operational success of CommonSpirit Health’s destination care program in partnership with clinical, financial, and internal and external stakeholders – serving patients traveling 150 or more miles for specialty care, from neighboring communities across the United States to international markets. The Director advances program performance, team excellence, and a concierge-caliber patient experience, ensuring every patient experiences frictionless care from first inquiry through return home. This role is suited to a self-driven leader who thrives in a fast-paced environment and brings strong team leadership, process improvement skills, and comfort leading teams through change. The ideal candidate leads with adaptability, resourcefulness, and a collaborative spirit, and is deeply committed to delivering an exceptional experience for every destination care patient. This is an in-person, onsite role.

**Job Description**
-------------------

OBJECTIVES/PURPOSE

 

* Builds and leads Takeda’s new Central Laboratory Operations group, defining the vision, operating model, organizational design, capabilities, and ways of working required to deliver enterprise technical and operational oversight of central laboratory services across global clinical development programs.
* Establishes the foundational infrastructure for central laboratory oversight, including processes, vendor strategy, systems, and metrics, so that central laboratory solutions are technically sound, operationally executable, globally compliant, and inspection-ready from study design through database lock and study closeout.
* Provides leadership of the Sample Management group, ensuring its in-trial activities interface effectively with central laboratory operations. Biorepository and biobank activities are out of scope for this role.
* Partners with Clinical Science, Clinical Operations, Translational Medicine, Translational Biomarkers and Bioanalytics, Data Management, Biometrics, Regulatory Affairs, Quality, Procurement, and external laboratory providers to deliver consistent, scalable central laboratory capabilities across the portfolio.

ACCOUNTABILITIES

 

**Building the Central Laboratory Operations Group (primary focus)**

* Define and execute the vision, strategy, and multi-year roadmap to stand up the Central Laboratory Operations group, including mission, scope, service model, phased capability build, and measures of success.
* Design the organizational structure, roles, and resourcing plan; recruit, onboard, develop, and lead a high-performing team of central laboratory technical and operational experts.
* Establish the central laboratory operating model and oversight framework, including standards, decision rights (RACI), governance forums, escalation pathways, and interfaces with Clinical Operations, Translational Medicine, Translational Biomarkers and Bioanalytics, Data Management, Biometrics, Quality, and Procurement.
* Develop the foundational processes, SOPs, work instructions, templates, and training needed to standardize central laboratory startup, conduct, and closeout across studies, and transition existing study-level central laboratory activities into the new group without disruption to ongoing studies.
* Develop the business case, budget, and resource forecasts for the group, and secure leadership alignment and sponsorship for the phased build-out.
* Lead the central laboratory vendor strategy, including evaluation, selection, and qualification of central laboratories and will consult in evaluation and selection of specialty laboratories as appropriate, technical capability assessments, quality and compliance reviews, contracting input with Procurement, service-level expectations, KPIs, issue escalation, and ongoing vendor governance.
* Provide technical oversight during clinical development planning and protocol design by assessing laboratory feasibility, test menus, specimen requirements, reference ranges, turnaround times, and the operational impact of study endpoints and schedules.
* Establish central laboratory systems and data capabilities, including laboratory information management systems, electronic data capture interfaces, data transfer specifications, edit checks, result reconciliation, traceability, and data readiness for analysis, database lock, and regulatory submission.
* Build quality and regulatory compliance into the group from inception, including ICH-GCP, applicable GCLP principles, CLIA/CAP or equivalent laboratory requirements, data integrity, inspection readiness, audits, deviations, CAPAs, and vendor change controls. Lead IVDR requirements for each protocol.
* Establish portfolio-level central laboratory metrics, dashboards, and executive reporting for quality, timeliness, cost, risk, capacity, data delivery, and vendor performance; use trends and root-cause analysis to drive risk mitigation and sustained improvement.
* Drive modernization through standardized processes, automation, digital integration, data analytics, and emerging laboratory technologies as the group matures.

**Sample Management Group Oversight**

* Provide leadership of the Sample Management group, including setting priorities, allocating resources, approving goals, and supporting talent development; day-to-day sample management execution remains with the Sample Management lead.
* Define the handoffs between central laboratory operations and sample management (e.g., laboratory manuals, collection kits, sample shipment to central laboratories) so roles, responsibilities, and escalation paths are clear.
* Ensure appropriate sample management resourcing and integration at the study level to ensure end-to-end sample mgmt support during study conduct
* Serve as the senior escalation point for sample-related issues that affect central laboratory testing, study timelines, or data quality.

EDUCATION, EXPERIENCE, COMPETENCIES AND SKILLS

* Bachelor's degree in Life Sciences, Clinical Laboratory Science, Biomedical Science, Pharmacy, or a related field; advanced

degree such as MS, PhD, PharmD, or equivalent is preferred.

* 10+ years of experience in the pharmaceutical, biotechnology, central laboratory, diagnostic laboratory, or other regulated life-

sciences environment, with significant leadership responsibility for global clinical laboratory delivery.

* Proven track record of building a new function, team, or capability from the ground up, including defining strategy, operating

model, organizational design, processes, and governance.

* Demonstrated people leadership experience, including recruiting, developing, and managing teams and overseeing managers in

a matrixed global environment.

* Strong technical knowledge of central and specialty laboratory operations, service models, test menus, analytical platforms,

specimen requirements, reference intervals, laboratory workflow controls, and fit-for-purpose testing within clinical

development.

* Experience selecting, qualifying, contracting with, and governing global central laboratory vendors, including KPI/SLA

management, issue escalation, audits, CAPAs, and continuous improvement.

* Working knowledge of ICH-GCP, applicable GCLP principles, CLIA/CAP or equivalent laboratory standards, IVDR where

applicable, data integrity expectations, and global health authority inspection requirements.

* Strong knowledge of laboratory informatics and clinical technology, including LIMS, laboratory data standards, electronic data

capture interfaces, data transfer specifications, reconciliation, traceability, and data quality controls.

* General familiarity with clinical study sample management sufficient to lead the Sample Management group and manage

interfaces with central laboratory operations.

* Excellent strategic thinking, change leadership, risk management, communication, negotiation, vendor-management, and

executive presentation skills, with the ability to influence senior stakeholders across functions.
